Sample.evidence_source: Purposive sampling (five participants) and snowball sampling (two participants) were used, and thus, seven participants selected who had experienced suicidal thoughts following sexual violence.

Population.evidence_source: The research question of the study, 'what is the experience of male sexual violence survivors of suicidal ideation following sexual violence?', guided the selection of the sample. Purposive sampling (five participants) and snowball sampling (two participants) were used, and thus, seven participants selected who had experienced suicidal thoughts following sexual violence.

Type.evidence_source: The first author, who conducted all the interviews, tried to maintain an open mind and stay in 'the now' during the interviews, being ready to hear something new.

Area.evidence_source: The research question of the study, 'what is the experience of male sexual violence survivors of suicidal ideation following sexual violence?', guided the selection of the sample. ... All the participants said participating in the study was a relief for them. They felt it was good to be able to disclose their difficult experience where they were uninterrupted and could just tell their story. This said, they related that at the time of the interviews they experienced some strain and stress but afterwards they experienced relief and had greater well-being. They related this in the second interview. ... the men said that they experienced neither shame nor prejudice, which they related having been afraid of before the interviews.
